cq_coverage.details: All CQs are structurally supported by the ontology. Each question maps to appropriate classes (InvoiceMessage, Organization, AgentRole, Address, Item, Price, ReferenceNumber, BusinessProcess, etc.) and properties (hasRoleAssignment, involvesOrganization, hasAgentRole, hasAddress, hasLineItem, describesItem, hasPrice, hasNetPrice, hasInvoiceNumber, hasInvoiceAmount, hasMandatoryIdentifier, referencesBusinessProcess). No CQs are missing or only partially addressed.

strengths: Rich and deep class hierarchy, including pivot classes
Extensive use of restrictions and functional properties
Disjointness and disjointUnion axioms for key sections
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) for advanced logical patterns
Some disjointness could be strengthened (e.g., between AgentRole subtypes if modeled)
No use of property chains or SWRL rules for advanced validation

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain or range in some cases—though all major properties are covered)
P7 (Missing inverse properties for some data properties, but not required by OWL 2)

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add general class axioms (GCAs) for advanced validation (e.g., define InvoiceMessage as having at least one header, detail, and summary section, or use property chains to infer buyer/supplier roles).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enable richer automated reasoning and validation; improves ontology depth.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model AgentRole subclasses (e.g., Buyer, Supplier, DeliveryParty) and declare them disjoint.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Clearer role semantics and improved CQ clarity for role-based queries.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add explicit domain and range for all data properties, even if redundant, to avoid OOPS P4 warnings.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Cleaner OOPS/OntoClean reports and improved documentation.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add SKOS annotations for multilingual support or mapping to EN 16931 and P2P-O classes.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Better interoperability and documentation for European public procurement.

summary: The ontology provides a deep, well-structured model that covers all competency questions and aligns with best practices for EDIFACT invoice representation. It is OWL 2 compliant, uses pivot classes and functional properties effectively, and is annotation-rich. The main areas for improvement are the addition of general class axioms and more explicit role modeling, which would further enhance reasoning and validation capabilities.
